proof_review.conclusion: For any declared real PSD circulant K, an M-dimensional finite-second-moment Z exists. X_j=Z_(j mod M) makes each consecutive M-window a cyclic rotation, hence its covariance is K. One common X preserves all coincident samples. Sides can be independent blocks only as an extra modeled choice since their used sets are disjoint. Step M/2 yields two phases: left phases 0 and8192 with multiplicities4/3; right phases4096 and12288 with multiplicities3/3. Pointwise V=pq||d_even-d_odd||^2/n^2 implies (2). The construction imposes exact periodic repeats, not merely within-window circulant marginals.

Correct. Shared raw white six-vector yields d=(x0-x2,x2-x4), covariance [[2,-1],[-1,2]], mean variance1/2 and E[V]=3/2. Four latent coordinates with periodic repeats yield d=(z0-z2,z2-z0), covariance [[2,-2],[-2,2]], zero mean variance and E[V]=2. Both M=4 window marginals are I4 and share actual overlap coordinates. Thus the marginal-only contract does not identify a joint law; the design correctly avoids claiming multiple completions for every particular singular K.

Correct orientation. For a later start s+d, equal raw indices satisfy i=j+d; W_a W_(a+1)^T=J_d. Therefore Cov(d_a,d_(a+1))=sigma^2 A J_d A^T=sigma^2 C and the opposite block is C^T. All more distant blocks vanish in the explicitly selected raw-white model. Averaging centered covariances gives sigma^2[(n-1)Omega/n-(n-1)(C+C^T)/n^2]. Taking traces gives signed c with the stated2(n-1)/n^2 coefficient. This is distinct from stacked covariance and from a one-window trace.

Correct. J_d pairs the disjoint head indices0,...,T-d-1 and tail d,...,T-1, leaving middle indices unpaired. J_d+J_d^T is a direct sum of exchange2x2 blocks and zeros, so its eigenvalues belong to{-1,0,1}. Congruence gives -Omega<=C+C^T<=Omega. Substitution yields [(n-1)^2/n^2,(n^2-1)/n^2] times sigma^2 Omega and |c|<=g/2. Factors36/49,48/49 and25/36,35/36 are correct. No positive definiteness, inverse or Gaussianity is required; zero/singular cases remain valid.

Correctly separates true A from coefficient midpoint rows/Gram. Four endpoint products bound each scalar shifted product; exact outward summation is valid despite coefficient dependence, though may be conservative. Full retained coefficient intervals are required to compute c; scalar g bounds or hashes cannot supply it. This source packet performs no such integration.

Correct. Centering realized windows removes their realized mean, not the mean-dispersion contribution in expectation. True A annihilates a common constant nominal raw mean, but arbitrary drift/signal means need explicit treatment. A general calibration map need not preserve constants. Signed overlap remains after an n/(n-1) rescaling. No calibration envelope, eta, stationarity or distribution law is inferred from RI116.

Correct as an absolute covariance-contribution difference for symmetric Delta=Sigma_true-Sigma_model and a supplied eta>=0 with ||Delta||_2<=eta. Set K=D^T Pi D>=0. The inequalities -eta I<=Delta<=eta I give |tr(K Delta)|<=eta tr(K)=eta||Pi D||_F^2. Means and other model discrepancies remain separate.

Correct as an absolute bound on the change in the specified calibrated-Z covariance contribution. With U=T_c C_0 F and V=T_c Delta_C F, the difference is [2<U,V>_F+||V||_F^2]/n; Cauchy-Schwarz gives the stated bound. This requires one fixed factor covariance F F^T and additive calibration perturbation. Noise covariance, signal mean and dependent cross terms are not included automatically.
